name: Globe and Mail cryptic crossword No 3,334

indicatorNotes.about: IRATE goes about, around, the note

blocks.note: TE, a note of the sol-fa scale, sits inside IRATE as I-TE-RATE

annotation.surface: A well-schooled Liberal politician seething over a memo.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Note' reads as a written message, but it is a sol-fa note, which splits the word for fuming after its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone literate is educated, able to read and write.

indicatorNotes.avoids: MOSES avoids the E, leaving it out

annotation.surface: A prophet steering clear of a power station.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Energy plant' looks like a power station; split it, and energy is the E to drop while plant is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: plant is the broad category, and the answer is one of its simplest flowerless members.

entries.clue: Revolutionary saint ousting one in Egyptian capital (6)

indicatorNotes.ousting: ST ousts the I, taking its place

blocks.note: I = one, the letter swapped out

annotation.surface: A radical holy man displacing someone in Cairo.
annotation.walkthrough: Fidel Castro led the Cuban revolution; the clue's 'saint' and 'Revolutionary' sit oddly together, which is the joke of the surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Fidel Castro is the archetypal revolutionary leader.

indicatorNotes.under: in a down clue, DEN comes under DRY

blocks.note: a den is a study, a private room

annotation.surface: Reading the work of a tedious author.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Boring' suggests drilling but means dull; 'under' works only because this is a down entry. John Dryden was an English poet and playwright.
annotation.definitionFit: John Dryden, the seventeenth-century poet laureate, is a major literary figure.

annotation.surface: A politician seen to be in distress.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shown suffering' reads as one phrase; the break falls between them, with 'shown' giving AIRED as in a programme aired on TV.
annotation.definitionFit: Impaired means damaged or weakened, suffering some loss of function.

entries.clue: Sport in lake amid rising mist (4)

indicatorNotes.in: in means placed inside, so the lake goes within the mist
indicatorNotes.amid: L sits amid the letters of FOG
indicatorNotes.rising: in a down clue, rising turns FOG upward to GOF

annotation.surface: A game played on a lake in rising mist.
annotation.walkthrough: The container is read before the reversal: FOG rises to GOF, then L goes inside.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: the sport named is the one played with clubs on a course.

entries.clue: Cooked tinamou right for Maze prisoner? (8)

indicatorNotes.Cooked: cooked food is transformed, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: Serving a roast game bird to someone locked in a maze.
annotation.walkthrough: A tinamou is a South American game bird, so the kitchen picture holds; the question mark flags the playful definition.
annotation.definitionFit: The Minotaur of Greek myth was kept in the Labyrinth on Crete, a maze prisoner.

indicatorNotes.onset: the onset of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do

annotation.surface: A description of a gloomy spell setting in.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Low' as a feeling is a false lead: it is the verb for a cow's call. Read whole, the clue describes a low mood, which is why 'This' stands for the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: A low spell as depression begins is a mood, a bad one.

entries.clue: Debt is restructured for small home (6)

annotation.surface: Rescheduling a loan so someone can afford a tiny flat.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Is' does double service: it is part of the fodder and also reads naturally with 'restructured'. A bedsit is British for a one-room rented flat.
annotation.definitionFit: A bedsit, a single room for sleeping and living, is a small home.

entries.clue: Happy maybe appearing in Cold War fiction (5)

indicatorNotes.appearing in: the answer appears inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: A cheerful character in a spy novel.
annotation.walkthrough: Happy is capitalised as a sentence opener, disguising the name: he is one of Snow White's seven dwarfs, and 'maybe' marks him as an example.
annotation.definitionFit: Happy is one of the seven dwarfs in Snow White.

blocks.note: the French word for a street
an old verb for being sorry about something

annotation.surface: The Gallic manner of apologising.
annotation.walkthrough: 'French way' seems to mean a French style of doing things; it is a literal way, a street, as in Rue de Rivoli.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is French vocabulary for a street; the second is an English verb meaning to be sorry for.

entries.clue: Bachelor stopping to look round summerhouse (6)

indicatorNotes.stopping: B stops, plugs, the gap between GAZE and O

annotation.surface: A single man pausing to look around a garden shelter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Look round' reads as one phrase meaning survey; split it, and round is the O that follows GAZE.
annotation.definitionFit: A gazebo is a summerhouse, an open garden pavilion.

indicatorNotes.developed: the letters are developed into a new form

annotation.surface: A drug-fuelled moment of joyful insight.
annotation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word joining 'developed' to 'happy', but its letters belong in the fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the secular sense: a sudden flash of insight, borrowed from the religious feast of revelation.

indicatorNotes.keeping: keeping means holding something safe inside, so the phrase for impossible holds the rook

annotation.surface: A Swede's neighbour who can't be persuaded to keep a chess piece.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Neighbour' suggests a person next door; it is a country.
annotation.definitionFit: A geographical definition: the country sharing Sweden's long western border.

entries.clue: Christian figure, a genius, worked with duke (5,3)

indicatorNotes.worked: the letters are worked into a new shape

annotation.surface: A brilliant artist collaborating with a nobleman on a religious statue.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Figure' suggests a person; the Agnus Dei is an image, the Lamb of God.
annotation.definitionFit: The Agnus Dei, Lamb of God, is a Christian figure for Christ.

entries.clue: Soldiers for example eaten by fierce creature (6)

indicatorNotes.eaten by: EG is eaten, swallowed inside LION

annotation.surface: Troops being devoured by a wild beast.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Roman soldiers thrown to the lions, a picture that hides a plain container.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: originally a Roman army unit, now any large body of soldiers.

entries.clue: No green light, that is, for Congress (6)

blocks.note: a green light is the OK

annotation.surface: Parliament refusing approval for a bill.
annotation.walkthrough: Capitalised Congress looks like the US legislature; here it is sexual congress, and nookie is slang for sex.
annotation.definitionFit: Congress in the sense of sexual intercourse is nookie in slang.

indicatorNotes.in: in means placed within, so the clamour goes inside the smoke

blocks.note: fag is British slang for a cigarette

annotation.surface: Noise dying away in a haze of smoke.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Smoke' is a noun for a cigarette, which in British slang is a fag.
annotation.definitionFit: Fading means growing fainter, becoming less.

blocks.note: a jaguar is a big cat; the question mark marks the example

annotation.surface: A wealthy executive riding in a big Jaguar car.
annotation.walkthrough: Jaguar is capitalised for the luxury car a fat cat might drive, but it is the animal.
annotation.definitionFit: A fat cat is a rich, powerful person, a big shot.

indicatorNotes.reportedly: as reported, spoken, so the sound counts

blocks.note: surplus as in left over, in excess; said without its final R

annotation.surface: A glut of eggs, so they say.
annotation.walkthrough: The sound match relies on a non-rhotic accent, where OVER drops its final R.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in Latin plural form: the scientific word for egg cells, a crossword favourite.

blocks.note: the brutish humans in Gulliver's Travels by Jonathan Swift
an early internet search and news site

annotation.walkthrough: Jonathan Swift coined 'Yahoo' for the savage humans in Gulliver's Travels, and the web company borrowed the name.
annotation.definitionFit: The first sense is Swift's coinage for boorish humans; the second is the internet company that borrowed the name.

entries.clue: Yankee beer in New Haven university (4)

blocks.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet

annotation.surface: A New Englander drinking beer at college.
annotation.walkthrough: The Yankee and the beer fit a campus bar scene, which keeps the letters Y and ALE out of sight.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by location: the Ivy League institution sits in New Haven, Connecticut.

indicatorNotes.in: in means placed within, so the drug goes inside the confidence

annotation.surface: Dealing drugs on the quiet.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Push' and 'heroin' paint a drug dealer, and 'in confidence' sounds like secrecy, yet it is TRUST holding H.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym as a verb: to shove forcefully.

entries.clue: Said to be in power shower (4)

indicatorNotes.Said: said aloud, so the sound counts

blocks.note: to reign is to be in power

annotation.surface: Talk of a powerful shower head.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Power shower' is a strong household shower; split it, and power belongs to the wordplay while shower is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a shower is one brief form that water falling from clouds takes.

indicatorNotes.in: in prison means locked inside, so the 50 goes within the prison word

blocks.note: the can is slang for prison

annotation.surface: A large family with fifty members behind bars.
annotation.walkthrough: The number 50 is read as the Roman numeral L.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym: a word of Scottish origin for a group of related families.

entries.clue: Fancied a military man in tight denim (8)

indicatorNotes.in: A GI goes in the rearranged denim
indicatorNotes.tight: tight means drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier

annotation.surface: Admiring a soldier in snug jeans.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tight' fits the jeans in the surface but means drunk, the anagram signal for DENIM.
annotation.definitionFit: Plain synonym in the past tense: fancied in the sense of pictured in the mind.
